channel.title: Danesh Morales Hashemi — Blog
channel.description: Notes on quantum information, mathematics, and research.

item.title: Constructing Qubit Channels with Arbitrary Fixed Points
item.description: Motivated by the Banach fixed-point theorem, we construct a single-qubit channel, a rotated convex combination of the depolarizing and amplitude damping channels, whose repeated application drives any initial state to any chosen target state. Includes an interactive Bloch-sphere explorer of the trajectory.

item.title: Introduction to Cycle Benchmarking for Quantum Error Diagnostics
item.description: A scalable, SPAM-robust protocol for estimating the process fidelity of a fixed cycle of parallel gates. We introduce the CB protocol, explain how randomized compiling tailors noise into Pauli channels, and analyze when the gate-independence assumption can be relaxed.

item.title: Self-Consistent Gauges for Cycle Benchmarking under Gate-Dependent Noise
item.description: When the randomizing gates of cycle benchmarking have gate-dependent errors, its estimates fall far below their targets. Comparing against a gauge-rotated target, built from the leading Kraus operator of an averaged channel, closes much of the gap. We also show why randomized compiling still tailors gate-dependent easy-gate noise into Pauli channels.

item.title: Superoperator Representations and the Characterization of Completely Positive Maps
item.description: Six ways to write a quantum channel (Kraus operators, Stinespring dilations, Liouville and Pauli transfer matrices, Choi matrices and χ-matrices), how to convert between them, and how complete positivity and trace preservation look in each. Based on my AMATH 900 project at the University of Waterloo.
